title: Wrap a cable tie round three hanging cords, thread it and pull it snug
instruction: Close the cable tie snugly around the three cords, then let go of it.
context: Cords hanging under a TV get bundled with a nylon cable tie. Nothing here is set up for it: the tie lies on the console in front of the cords. It has to be picked up, passed behind the cords, both ends brought round to the front, the 3 mm tip fed into the slot in the head from the correct side, and the tail pulled until the loop closes on them. It takes both hands throughout: the strap springs straight when let go, and the tail only draws through while the other hand holds the head.
setup: Table coordinates in metres: x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y left from the midline, z up from the console top; the arm bases are at y = +0.305 (left) and y = -0.305 (right). The console is the table. A painted drywall wall stands across its far side, front face at x = 0.460, 60 cm wide and 42 cm tall. A TV hangs on the wall, stood in for by its black bottom edge (a box 4 cm deep, 60 cm wide, 8 cm tall), its bottom 34 cm above the console. A white plastic power strip (28 x 5.5 x 4 cm) lies on the console centred at (0.400, 0.000), its long side along y. Three cords run straight down from the TV's bottom edge to the top of the power strip (30 cm), gathered in a bundle: a black PVC TV power cord (7.0 mm diameter, axis at x 0.379, y -0.004), a black PVC HDMI cable (7.3 mm, at 0.379, +0.004) and a white TPE phone charger cable (3.5 mm, at 0.383, 0.000). A black nylon 6/6 cable tie (strap 369 x 4.8 x 1.2 mm with a tapered last 6 mm, sold as 370 mm; head 8 x 9 x 5.6 mm with a slot through it; about 2.8 g) lies flat on the console in front of the power strip: its head centred at (0.290, -0.170) with the slot vertical, its strap straight along +y, its tip at y = 0.203. Two white paint marks, each a 2.5 mm band across the strap, are centred 290 mm and 270 mm from the tip. Nothing holds the tie: no stand, no clip, no loop made beforehand.
scoring: Checked on the real setup by eye, with a photo and a 1 s video, after the arms let go. 0 unless both grippers are at least 3 cm from the tie, the tie is still (no part of it moved more than 1 cm over the last second), its tail has come at least 2 mm out of the head's far side and all three cords pass through the loop. Then 1.0 if the centre of the mark 290 mm from the tip has come out of the head's far side; 0.5 if the centre of the mark 270 mm from the tip has; 0.25 otherwise (closed round the cords, but loose). A mark is out when its 2.5 mm band shows whole beyond the head's far face or is cut by it past its middle: a reading to the millimetre. With the 290 mm mark at the face, 73 mm of strap is left in the loop (the three cords hugged take 36 mm); with the 270 mm mark, 93 mm. The marks are minimums: a tie drawn further, down onto the cords, scores the same. Success, which ends the trial, is the 1.0 condition held for 1 s. The simulation reads the same quantities from the strap's link chain: the tail is the strap's length past the slot's exit face, a cord passes through the loop when its axis lies inside the loop's outline, and clearance is measured from each gripper's TCP and pad tips.
reset_notes: A closed tie can only come off by cutting it, so each trial uses a new 370 x 4.8 mm tie from the same bag, marked 290 mm and 270 mm from its tip with a paint pen against a steel rule and laid flat at the start position. The cords and the power strip do not move.
fidelity: The strap is 59 rigid 6.25 mm links on bending joints with nylon's stiffness, 15 times heavier and damped for stability: flat it droops, on edge it stands out as a real tie does. Friction by contact: strap on the pads 0.9, in the slot 0.25, on the cords 0.35. The slot is 6.4 x 4.0 mm with a 0.5 mm lead-in (real: about 5.2 x 1.6). The ratchet is a sprung pawl; code holds it clear until 8 mm of tail is out and stiffens it when the strap backs out. The cords are rigid. More in the README.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0; demo: 1.0 (scripted; it reads the simulator's state)
